libertine · Nov 21, 2026

I tie this with collectibles market, where people want to compress the experience of decades into waves of months. It's completely fake.

People used to play and had fun with their toys, a small fraction took better care because there was something about it that was worth treasuring - not because they could resell it in the future, but because of what it represented, usually a memory.

That's where scarcity of collectibles used to come from.

Most people had to be lucky to have something in a special occasion.

Now people turned this upsidedown and they're not even having memories with their toys, and companies are feeding into this.

Or they buy stuff to keep it boxed in, we're talking about toys. I used to save the boxes of the toys I cherished the most, but I played the hell out of them.

Now it's gambling, or artificial scarcity, or what ever this is that's completely hollow. There's no moment attached to it.

I really struggle to understand this behavior, I mean, I get it but I don't understand how people play into it without feeling something is off.
